transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Rylan Barton.
President Trump says he ordered the Justice Department lawsuit over Alaska's Senate race.
In an appearance with Florida Republican Governor Ron DeSantis, Trump said his administration
sued to block certification of the election if his favorite candidate, incumbent Republican
Senator Dan Sullivan, loses.
I'm the one that said do it.
I have two guys run, named Dan Sullivan running.
So the Democrats put up a guy never, I don't think he ever voted before, all of a sudden
he decides to run.
An unaffiliated candidate, also named Dan Sullivan, is on the ballot, along with Democrat
Mary Peltola.
The Alaska Supreme Court previously rejected efforts to remove the other Sullivan.
The lawsuit has sparked concerns about a lengthy battle between the federal government and
states over election certification.
Russia's government says that the first tanker-carrying Russian diesel to the U.S. has set sail under
a new import agreement.
It comes two weeks after President Trump announced the deal with President Vladimir Putin despite
Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
Energy experts say the agreement is unlikely to lower fuel prices.
The French government is deploying 70,000 police to secure streets during tomorrow's
protest marches.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley reports there's a curfew for minors in several cities, including
parts of Paris.
The Louvre and several other major Paris museums will be closed Saturday.
Many Paris shopkeepers, still reeling from the destruction and violence of last weekend,
have boarded up their stores.
In Lyon, Nice and Montpellier, marches have been banned for security reasons.
In Paris, authorities have diverted some protest routes away from shopping streets and public
buildings to limit possible damage.
President Emmanuel Macron, who has been criticized for being absent from the crisis, met with
high school students for the first time to hear their grievances.
He said the government would work with them to find solutions.
But critics say he has already lost French youth.
Eleanor Beardsley in Pierre News, Paris.
Drugmaker Merck has released early some much-awaited clinical data looking at the effectiveness
of mRNA vaccine and the serious skin cancer melanoma.
The data show the vaccine treatment can substantially slow down both the recurrence of the cancer
and death from it, and Pierre's Yuki Noguchi reports Merck and its partner Moderna will
use the data to apply for regulatory approval.
The medical community has been awaiting release of this data, which is the largest study to
date gauging the effectiveness of mRNA vaccine technology against cancer.
In this case, vaccines are designed and personalized based on each person's melanoma tumor sample.
Over the two-year study period, those drugs reduced the risk of occurrence or death among
patients by 42 percent compared to the standard immunotherapy treatment alone.
Moreover, the study found that adding the vaccine did not increase significant side
effects.
Yuki Noguchi, NPR News.
Major U.S. stock indexes fell today.
The Dow fell nearly one and a quarter percent.
This is NPR News.
President Trump is exempting some imports, including plywood, sheets, packing crates
and some machinery from the 50 percent tariffs on Canadian products.
The exemptions could help main Republican Senator Susan Collins in her reelection battle
against Democratic challenger Troy Jackson.
The White House said the president was seeking to offset "the burden to U.S. commerce while
better serving the public interest."
The World Series starts tonight between the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays, and
Pierre's Becky Sullivan reports neither has ever won a championship.
More than a decade of champions from large markets like Los Angeles and Houston, this
World Series is a match-up of two small-budget teams.
Milwaukee's payroll ranks number 19 in baseball, Tampa number 28.
These teams were powerhouses this season each.
The top team and their respective league both get their money's worth from rosters that
can play whatever kind of baseball is needed, such as walks, singles, stolen bases, great
defense, great pitching.
Here's Rays outfielder Chandler Simpson.
For sure it's gonna be a dogfight.
I mean, it's gonna be the best of who can play their game the best.
It's like looking in the mirror, honestly.
It's the first time since 1980 that neither team in the World Series has ever won it.
The Rays were last in the World Series in 2020.
For the Brewers, it's been since 1982.
Becky Sullivan and Pierre News, Milwaukee.
And qualification for the first ever World Treadmill Championship has begun.
Created by a company called Run X, runners have until January to log a 5K on a treadmill
at an official Run X center around the world.
They compete for a $100,000 prize.
A regional phase begins at the end of January, and the finals are in March.
I'm Rylan Barton, you're listening to NPR News from Washington.

topics.text: President Trump says he ordered Justice Department lawsuit over Alaska Senate race, backing Dan Sullivan
Russia says first tanker carrying Russian diesel to U.S. sets sail under new import deal
French government deploys 70,000 police ahead of nationwide protest marches; Paris museums closing Saturday
Merck releases early data showing mRNA melanoma vaccine slows cancer recurrence and death
Major U.S. stock indexes fall, with the Dow dropping nearly 1.25 percent
Trump exempts plywood, packing crates and some machinery from 50 percent tariffs on Canadian goods
Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays open World Series tonight, neither having won a championship
Run X announces qualification for first-ever World Treadmill Championship, with $100,000 prize
